{{< include _head.qmd >}}

Fifteen examples from Stefan Kostka, Dorothy Payne and Byron Almén's *Tonal Harmony*: chapter 18, "Modulations Using Diatonic Common
Chords", and chapter 19, "Some Other Modulatory Techniques". Most are from real pieces (Bach, Mozart, Beethoven, Schubert, Dvořák,
Tchaikovsky); 18-2, 18-3a and 18-3b are short progressions.

How to read the labels and use the scores: [Analysed Scores](index.qmd#reading-the-labels). For modulation itself, see
[Chapter 22](../modulation.qmd).

{{< include _kostka-payne.qmd >}}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## For teachers

- **Source:** the notes and analyses are the DDMAL Key Modulation Dataset's encodings of the book's examples (Néstor Nápoles López and
  others), translated automatically to RomanText and copied into When in Rome. `scripts/when-in-rome/build.mjs` reads the MusicXML
  (`src/kostka`), and every note was checked against music21's reading of the same files.
- **Copyright:** the book is in copyright. The pieces are public domain; 18-2, 18-3a and 18-3b are progressions as encoded in the
  dataset, and 19-12 is the book's simplification of bars 6–16 of Mozart's Fantasia, K. 475.
- **Not shown:** grace notes (19-1, 19-3) are left out of the scores.
- **Not edited:** the analyses are an automated translation and are shown as they are.
:::
